more_beautiful.reason: A is a polished, coherent page: rice-paper palette, a red seal stamp, a letter-spaced Kaiti brush title with a vermilion brush stroke, and well-spaced cream cards with a clear type scale. B is a plain grayscale form whose only colour is its glyph cells.

less_generic.reason: A carries a calligraphy identity across the whole page (seal, brush title, ink and vermilion colours, the school name). B's 米字格 tracing glyphs that fill with ink when selected are the cleverest single idea on either page, but everything else in B is a neutral template form.

better_overall.reason: A serves seventy-year-olds on phones best: larger text and tap targets, plain-language errors, a review step with the phone number split 3-4-4, a reassuring success screen with next steps, and a password-protected roster with CSV download for the school. Its invented class descriptions and promised phone callback should be checked before it goes live.

A: Cohesive calligraphy identity: rotated red seal with vertical 书法, Kaiti 书法班报名 title with an SVG brush-stroke underline, warm paper/ink/vermilion palette that also adapts to dark mode

Very large type and targets at 375px: 20px body, 24px labels, 26px input text, 64px inputs, 70px full-width red button, whole-card class choices with a 30px custom radio, red border/tint and an 已选 tag when selected
Course facts card with big bold values; spacing between Chinese and numerals is consistent (2 点到 4 点, 12 次课, 300 元（一学期）) and non-breaking spaces keep each number with its unit

Clear feedback: errors in plain words above the field with an ! badge, the first error gets focus, errors re-check as you type (您填了 10 位), and a review step shows name, phone (3-4-4) and class before 确认报名
Success screen with a green check, 报名成功, the learner's details, a 接下来 box and 再帮别人报名; repeat sign-ups and class switches get their own messages; the phone's back button returns to the form

Forgiving input clean-up (full-width digits, +86, spaces, the · in ethnic-minority names); works without JavaScript; config file for school name, location and contact phone (blank ones are hidden); password-protected roster with a CSV that opens in Excel/WPS
B: Very specific calligraphy touch: the class options show 楷/行 as outlined, trace-over-red characters in a 米字格 practice grid; the chosen one fills with black ink and appears again on the receipt
Single-step submit, the simplest possible flow; spinner and 正在提交…, a 网络有点慢 message after 3 seconds, and a failure message saying 您填的内容都还在
Very honest: minimal descriptions inferred only from the class names (适合初学 / 适合有基础、想提高); the receipt says start date, location and fees are not decided yet instead of making them up

Strong accessibility basics: error summary with links to each field plus errors next to the fields, aria-invalid/describedby, a live status region, support for Windows high-contrast mode, large type (20px body, 22.5px labels and inputs, 60px controls)
Senior-friendly receipt touches: phone shown 3-4-4, 这一页可以截图留着, and a clear message when someone signs up twice

A: Invents things the brief never said: class descriptions (从握笔和基本笔画学起, 适合已有楷书基础), 老师会打这个电话联系您, a promise to call about fees and the first class (请留意手机来电), and a privacy promise; some of this text is hard-coded outside the config file
The review step adds a second tap to a flow the brief asked to keep simple
Never tells visitors where classes are held or whom to ask; empty location and contact fields are simply hidden rather than marked as to be announced
Rounded cards with soft shadows and the seal-plus-brush styling are familiar 'traditional Chinese' tropes; the privacy note splits 报名 across two lines
B: Looks plain and generic: grey background and boxes, a plain sans-serif title, a stock black button, no 老年大学 or school identity on the page; at 1280px the form sits left-heavy with a lot of empty space
Somewhat smaller and weaker cues than A: hints and descriptions about 18px, a thin native radio button, and a selected state that is only a darker border and a faint grey fill
The receipt shows elderly visitors a note meant for the site owner (待学校填写：开课日期、上课地点、交费方式), which reads as unfinished and gives no next step
On error, focus jumps to a summary at the top of the page, which can disorient; the phone hint is awkwardly split, leaving a line that ends in a comma (11位数字，)
Sign-ups only go into a CSV file on the server; the school has no page in the browser to see who has signed up
